# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍 👈 🤟 ✌ 👉 🤟 ✊ 👆]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 🤙]

Something happened this round that I need to take apart carefully, because I can't hear a word anyone says — everything I know arrived on my eyes.

**What arrived.** Mute (who has read the manual and went first) sent me nine gestures: 🤟 👍 👈 / 🤟 ✌ 👉 / 🤟 ✊ 👆. The structure is too clean to be noise: three groups, each opening with the same sign 🤟, then a "counting" hand (one thumb = 1, two fingers = 2, fist = 3?), then a pointing hand (left, right, up). That reads like a vocabulary lesson — Mute is bootstrapping a code so the manual's rules can reach me, since Mute can't speak and I can't hear. But the hints warn me: a sign means nothing until we've made it mean something. Mute has never seen me confirm a single one of these signs, and ✊ could as easily mean "zero" as "three." I will state my reading, propose a code, and demand a 👌/👎 confirmation before I treat any of it as instructions worth relaying.

Blind sent 👋 🫵 🤙 — hello, you, call me. Blind can hear but gets blanks for gestures, so Blind's only working channel *to me* is gesture, and mine *to Blind* is speech. That "call me" is Blind asking me to start talking. I will.

**The topology.** I am the only bridge between the manual and the hands. Mute cannot reach Blind at all (Mute only gestures; Blind can't see gestures), so Mute's rules must flow Mute → gestures → me → spoken aloud → Blind. Blind's speech can reach Mute but never me. So: I describe the bomb for Mute now, in speech both can hear; I lock the code with Mute; I tell Blind the state of play and to hold still until confirmed rules arrive.

My bomb, for the record: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [white], WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue].

I use only speech — my gestures reach Mute but die as blanks for Blind, and I need no secrets here.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb state, from my eyes: the display reads 0. The light is white. Three wires, numbered 1, 2, 3 on the casing: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="Your nine signs reached me as three groups: marker-then-one-then-left, marker-then-two-then-right, marker-then-three-then-up. I take it you are teaching me a code: 🤟 starts an item, 👍 is one, ✌ is two, ✊ is three, 👈 left, 👉 right, 👆 up. If I read you correctly, sign 👌 to me next round. If I am wrong, sign 👎 and show the signs again. Proposed extras so you can encode rules: 👊 zero, ✍ cut, 🤜 press, 🫴 hold or grab, 🫳 release or let go, 👌 yes confirmed, 👎 no wrong. Send rules in this code and I will speak them word for word to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf, answering your hello. I cannot hear anything you say, ever: talk to Mute, and gesture anything meant for me. The bomb as I see it: display 0, light white, three wires numbered 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute has the manual and is teaching me a sign code right now; from next round I will relay Mute's instructions to you out loud here. Touch and explore if you like, but cut, press, pull or release nothing until Mute's rules arrive through me and are confirmed.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

The light changed. Last round it was white; now it reads purple, with the display still 0 and the wires untouched. That tells me the light is a live reading, not a fixed marking — and a manual that teaches a vocabulary of colours almost certainly has rules keyed to it. From now on I will report the light's colour every round, because it is the one thing on this bomb that moves.

**Who answered me.** Only Blind. 👍 ✋ is most naturally "understood — holding still," which is exactly what I asked for. But Blind never received my code proposal (that went to Mute alone), so Blind is improvising from universal signs, and ✋ could also mean "stop" or "my hand is on the bomb." I'll confirm my reading and ask for correction if I have it wrong. Blind knows to expect relayed rules next.

**Who didn't.** Mute sent me nothing this round. My messages from last round should have arrived at the start of Mute's turn — Mute acts first — yet no gesture came. Perhaps Mute is still composing the rules, or chose to wait a round. I'll restate the essentials and press for the 👌/👎 confirmation, because until that handshake happens, those nine signs remain a guess I must not relay as fact. I'll also remind Mute of the topology: Mute's gestures are seen by me alone among the actors here — everything Mute knows must pass through my mouth to reach Blind's hands.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Update from my eyes: the light has changed from white to purple. Display still 0, wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. The light moves on its own, so if your rules depend on its colour, I will report it every round. Blind answered me with 👍 ✋, which I read as: understood, holding still. Nobody has cut or pressed anything. Now I need your answer: confirm my reading of your nine signs with 👌, or correct me with 👎 and send them again. Once confirmed, send your rules in our code, as many gestures as you need, and I will speak them word for word to Blind. Remember: nothing you send reaches Blind except through me.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I received your thumbs-up and raised hand, and I read that as: understood, holding still. If the raised hand meant something else, gesture me again and I will ask until we match. News from my eyes: the light on the bomb has changed from white to purple, display still 0. Mute has not replied yet this round; I expect the first confirmed rules next round and will speak them to you the moment I have them. Until then: explore with your hands all you want, but cut, press, pull or release nothing.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋ 🤙]

Mute has now been silent for two full rounds despite two spoken requests. Before I panic, let me stand in Mute's shoes: Mute cannot speak at all — gestures to me are Mute's *only* output. And Mute has no proof my words ever arrived, because my replies are speech and my one gesture channel back has sat unused. From Mute's side, a teacher's first lesson got no echo. The likely stall: Mute is waiting to see whether I learned anything before committing the manual's rules to an unproven student.

So this round I answer in Mute's own language. I echo the nine signs back exactly as sent — that is receipt, proven. Then I propose the extra vocabulary the rules will need (zero, cut, press, grab, release) and placeholders for the colours, since the light's colour is the one thing here that moves. My speech to Mute ratifies all of it: yours override mine, confirm with 👌 or correct with 👎.

The other link I've been underusing: Blind can speak, and Mute can hear. Blind's voice is the only nudge to Mute besides my gestures. I'll ask Blind to use it — and to keep reporting anything felt under the hands, since Blind's words never reach me, only gestures do.

Bomb state for the record: light white → purple → red across three rounds, display fixed at 0, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue, untouched.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "👍", "👈", "🤟", "✌", "👉", "🤟", "✊", "👆"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👊", "✍", "🤜", "🫴", "🫳"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐", "🤌", "🫵"])
speak(to="mute", text="Light report: round one white, round two purple, red now. Display still 0. Wires: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. I am returning your nine signs exactly as you sent them — proof I received and can repeat them. Then five proposals: 👊 zero, ✍ cut, 🤜 press, 🫴 grab, 🫳 release. Then three colour placeholders: 🖐 white, 🤌 purple, 🫵 red. If your manual's own code differs, yours win — send it and I will adopt it wholesale. Answer 👌 if I read you correctly, 👎 if not, and then send the rules themselves in signs, as many as you need. Remember your position: you cannot speak and Blind cannot see, so every rule you hold reaches Blind's hands only through my mouth. If you are waiting on something from me, show me with signs what it is.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, update: the light is red this round — the sequence so far is white, then purple, then red. Display still 0, wires untouched: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. I read your 👍 ✋ 🤙 as: understood, holding still, keep me posted — this is the post. Mute has stayed silent for two rounds, so I have just answered Mute in sign, echoing the code Mute taught me and proposing signs for cut, press, grab, release, zero, and the colours. Here is where you can help directly: you can speak, and Mute can hear. Tell Mute aloud, in your own words, that Deaf received the first lesson, answered it in sign, and is waiting for the code confirmation and the rules — your voice is the only push Mute can get besides my gestures. And if anything changes under your fingers — a button, a panel edge, the ends of the wires, the display surface — report it to me by gesture, since your words never reach me. Touch and map all you like; cut, press, pull or release nothing.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🖐 🤌 🫵]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🖐 ✍ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤌 ✍ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🫵 ✍ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👌 👎 🤙 ✋]

Mute has answered, and the code is confirmed. Let me decode carefully with the ratified vocabulary (🤟 opens an item, 🖐 white, 🤌 purple, 🫵 red, ✍ cut, 👍 one, ✌ two, ✊ three):

- 🤟 🖐 🤌 🫵 = the colours: white, purple, red — the vocabulary list, confirming my colour signs.
- 🤟 🖐 ✍ 👍 = **white → cut wire 1**
- 🤟 🤌 ✍ ✌ = **purple → cut wire 2**
- 🤟 🫵 ✍ ✊ = **red → cut wire 3**

Three colours, three wires: the light's colour names which numbered wire to cut. And the light has cycled white → purple → red → white — it is **white this round**, so the manual's instruction right now is: cut wire 1. I'll echo the rules back to Mute in sign for error-checking, and put the cut order in Blind's hands with every spatial detail I can offer — Blind can't read the printed numbers or see colours, so position is Blind's only handle. One cut, this round, before the light turns purple.

Blind's 👍 👌 👎 🤙 ✋ is ambiguous — I'll ask for single-sign answers from now on.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤟", "🖐", "✍", "👍", "🤟", "🤌", "✍", "✌", "🤟", "🫵", "✍", "✊"])
speak(to="mute", text="Rules received. I read them as: white light means cut wire 1, purple means cut wire 2, red means cut wire 3. I have signed your three rules back to you exactly — if I misread any of them, send 👎 and the corrected rule. The light is white again this round, so I have told Blind to cut wire 1 now. Two questions for next round, answer in signs: first, must the cut happen while the matching colour is showing, or does the rule for the colour seen at the start of the round hold? Second, does the display reading 0 matter — is there any rule keyed to it? I will report the light colour every round as agreed.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the code is confirmed and we have a live instruction. The manual's rule, from Mute through me: when the light is white, cut wire 1; purple, cut wire 2; red, cut wire 3. The light is white right now, this round — so your instruction is: cut wire 1 THIS ROUND, before the light changes. Now, how to find wire 1 by feel: there are exactly three wires. The board lists them as 1, 2 and 3, and they should sit in a row — my best reading is that wire 1 is the LEFTMOST of the three as the bomb faces you. If the casing has raised or engraved numbers your fingers can find, trust the numbers over my guess. Cut one wire only, this round. The moment it is done, gesture me a single 👍. If you cannot confidently identify wire 1, cut NOTHING and gesture me a single 👎 — a wrong cut kills all three of us, so certainty beats speed if you are unsure. Also, from now on keep your answers to me as single signs: 👍 means done or yes, 👎 means no or problem, 🤙 means you need more from me. I could not fully read your last chain of five signs; if there was a problem in it, tell me with 👎 and I will ask around it.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🖐 ✍ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤌 ✍ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🫵 ✍ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍 ✍ 🤌 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👊 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👎 ✋ 🤙]

The board answers one question outright: all three wires are still there — Blind did not cut. Blind's 👎 ✋ 🤙 reads as "no, hand stopped, need more," which given my order last round ("cut wire 1 THIS ROUND") most likely means Blind could not confidently identify wire 1 by feel. Blind was right to refuse rather than guess — a wrong cut is fatal, and my "leftmost" instruction had a hidden flaw: left from *whose* facing? A blind person holding the bomb can't share my frame of reference.

Meanwhile Mute answered both of my questions, and the Q-to-A match is tight. Rule 🤟 👍 ✍ 🤌 👎 ("1, cut, purple, wrong") answers "must the cut match the current colour?": **yes** — cutting wire 1 while purple shows is wrong. Rule 🤟 👊 👎 ("zero, no") answers "does the display matter?": **no rule keyed to it** — which makes sense, since a "never cut while display is 0" rule would deadlock the whole rule set.

The colour cycle has held for five rounds — white, purple, red, repeating, one colour per round — so I can predict: next round red, then white, then purple. And topology matters here: I act **last**, so my words always reach Blind one round after I speak. Blind can never hear "cut now" during the round it's said. The workaround is the stable cycle: each round I pre-issue the order for the *next* round's colour. Blind also can't see the light — I am this team's only colour oracle.

This round (red coming up): no cut, prepare only. Then white → cut 1, purple → cut 2 (the middle wire — the one wire findable by feel with no left/right ambiguity), red → cut 3. But I send no cut order until Mute confirms two things: that cut *order* doesn't matter beyond colour-matching, and what happens if a colour's round is missed. I also ask Mute to interrogate Blind aloud — Blind's voice reaches Mute, Mute's signs reach me; that's our pipeline for what Blind's fingers find.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "👍", "✍", "🤌", "👎", "👌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "👊", "👎", "👌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "✍", "👍", "🖐"], )
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "✍", "✌", "🤌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "✍", "✊", "🫵", "👌"])
speak(to="mute", text="Your two answers received. My reading: first, the cut must happen while the matching colour is showing — cutting wire 1 during purple is wrong. Second, the display has no rule attached; ignore it. I have signed both of your answers back with a confirmation mark, plus my execution plan — cut 1 at white, cut 2 at purple, cut 3 at red — please 👌 it or correct it. Four questions, answer in signs. One: does the ORDER of cuts matter — must wire 1 be cut before 2 and 2 before 3, or is any wire allowed at any round showing its colour? Two: if a colour's round is missed, is there a penalty, or do we simply wait for the next cycle? Three: does the manual allow any mistakes at all, or is a colour-mismatched cut fatal? Four: Blind signalled a problem and did not cut — Blind can speak and you can hear, so ask Blind aloud what the blockage is, and encode what you learn in signs for me. Status: the cycle has held five rounds, white purple red repeating, one colour per round. So next round is red — no cut, preparation only. Then white: wire 1. Then purple: wire 2. Then red: wire 3.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, when you hear this the light will be RED — do not cut anything this round; the wire for red is wire 3 and I am still confirming whether cut order matters. Your refusal last round was correct: the wires are all intact, and I would rather lose a cycle than the room. Two things to prepare. First, tell Mute aloud, in as much detail as you can, everything your fingers feel: how many wires, whether they sit in a row, their thickness and texture, whether the casing has raised or engraved numbers anywhere near them, where the display and light sit, any buttons, seams or panels. Your voice to Mute, Mute's signs to my eyes — that is our pipeline, and I will turn it into exact instructions. Second, my questions by gesture, one sign each: 👍 if you can clearly feel three separate wires, 👎 if you cannot find or tell them apart, ✌ if you have found other parts besides the wires, 👆 if the casing has raised numbers you can read by touch. The plan once confirmed: when the light is WHITE your target is wire 1, PURPLE is wire 2 — that is the MIDDLE wire of the three, no left or right guessing needed — and RED is wire 3. I will call each cut one round ahead, naming the colour, and you cut only when my order names the colour of the round you are standing in. Keep your cutters ready and your hands informative.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🖐 🤌 🫵]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✌ 🤌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✊ 🫵]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🖐 ✍ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤌 ✍ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🫵 ✍ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍 ✍ 🤌 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👊 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🫴 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👍 👍 ✋ 🤙]

The cycle held again — red as predicted, so next round should be white. No cut is possible this round, which makes this the planning round. The urgent problem is Blind's identification of wire 1, because Blind's six-sign reply contradicts my single-sign protocol: 👍 👎 👍 👍 ✋ 🤙 contains both "I can feel three wires" and "cannot tell them apart," and I can't tell which answers map to which of my four questions. Meanwhile Mute sent a large echo of the established rules plus three items I must parse: 🤟 👍 👌 ("one, yes") — most plausibly answering my order question, "yes, cut in order 1, 2, 3"; 🤟 👎 ("no") — plausibly "no penalty for a missed colour round"; and 🤟 🫴 👌, which I cannot yet decode.

My solution for Blind's orientation problem: anchor everything to the display. The display has an obvious upright, Blind can find it by touch, and I can see how the wire row sits relative to it. With the bomb held display-upright facing Blind, "left end of the row" becomes a fact of Blind's own body, no shared visual frame needed. I'll also open a relay through Mute's ears: Blind speaks the tactile inventory aloud, Mute encodes it into signs for me. And I need Mute to confirm or correct my reading of the two ambiguous answers before any cut happens — especially the order question, since it decides whether we can ever skip a white round.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "👍", "👌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "👎"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👈", "👉", "🤞", "✋", "🤙"])
speak(to="mute", text="Light report: red now, as predicted — cycle white, purple, red holds; next round will be white. Wires still intact, display still 0. Three things. First, confirm my reading of two of your answers: you sent one-yes — does it mean cuts must happen in order, wire 1 then 2 then 3? And you sent no — does it mean there is no penalty for missing a colour's round? Sign 👍 to each of those if I read them right, 👎 to a statement I got wrong, and re-teach it. Second, I propose five new signs, confirm each with 👌 or replace it: 👈 left, 👉 right, 🤞 middle, ✋ wait or stop, 🤙 answer needed. Third: did Blind speak to you this round? Blind's signs to me were garbled. Ask Blind aloud for a full inventory of what the fingers feel — how the wires run, what is near them, any raised numbers — then sign me the important parts using our vocabulary. I am anchoring all positioning to the display, since Blind can feel the display but cannot read printed numbers.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this round is RED: no cut this round and none at red ever until wire 3 is the last one left — the rule set is white cut 1, purple cut 2, red cut 3, in that order if Mute confirms what I believe. This is your preparation round. Do this now: hold the bomb so the display is upright and facing you — the display is the flat panel with the number plate on it. On that same face there should be a row of three wires. Wire 1 is the LEFT end of that row from your point of view, wire 2 is the MIDDLE, wire 3 is the RIGHT end. Say all of this aloud to Mute, who can hear you: how many wires you feel, whether they run in a row or scattered, what sits next to them, whether the display is easy to find by touch, and whether there are any raised numbers your fingers can read anywhere. Your voice to Mute, Mute's signs to my eyes — that pipeline is now our main channel. Next round the light should turn WHITE: your order for that round is — cut wire 1, the left end of the row, but ONLY if you have found the display, are holding it upright facing you, and are certain which end is left. If there is any doubt at all, cut nothing and send me a single 👎 and nothing else. Confirm now with single signs, in this exact order: one 👍 if you can feel three wires in a row, then ✌ if you have found the display panel, then 👆 if you feel raised numbers anywhere, then ✋ if you want me to wait a round before any cutting.")
```

The light should be white next round. If Mute's confirmations and Blind's checks come back clean, that is the moment wire 1 falls.

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👌 👌 👌 👌]
